Key facts As of 25 November 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), where community transmission is ongoing, has reported a total of 12 021 confirmed cases, including 5 904 related deaths (from data up until 24 November). Since the beginning of the outbreak, eight provinces have been affected: Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu, Tshopo, Haut-Uélé, Bas-Uélé, Sud Ubangi and Nord Ubangi. Since the beginning of the outbreak, excluding cases reported from DRC and those medically evacuated to Europe, 20 cases have been reported in Uganda, nine in Kenya and one in Nigeria (medically evacuated to Switzerland). Secondary transmission associated with imported cases has been reported in Uganda and Kenya. ECDC is monitoring the outbreak through its epidemic intelligence activities and actively liaising with partners to support the response. For more detailed epidemiological information and updates on the outbreak, visit ECDC’s Public health events page. Cases medically evacuated or imported to Europe Since May 2026, four cases of Ebola disease linked to the outbreak in DRC have been medically evacuated or imported to the European Union/European Economic Area (EU/EEA). Three patients were medically evacuated for specialised care, two to Germany and one to the Netherlands . A fourth case was reported in France in July. All four cases involved people working in healthcare or humanitarian roles in affected areas of DRC. In July, a resident of the United Kingdom (UK) was also evacuated to the UK following potential exposure while treating Ebola patients in DRC. On 26 October, a case reported in Nigeria and a close contact of hers were medically evacuated to Switzerland. On 5 November, a healthcare worker of British nationality working in DRC was medically evacuated to the UK. ECDC risk assessment On the basis of the available information, and given the uncertainties surrounding this outbreak, the likelihood of infection for people from the European Union/European Economic Area (EU/EEA) living in or travelling to affected areas is estimated to be low. Given the very low likelihood of importation and secondary transmission, the likelihood of infection for people living in the EU/EEA is estimated to be very low. This assessment will be reviewed as further information becomes available. Background Read more about the background of the outbreak .
